utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you, Mr. Kuehnel, of the affirmation you made, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could bring up P83, again, please. Mr. Kuehnel, this will again be the Law on Amnesty, which I think I showed you yesterday already. And I would ask the registry to go directly to page 2 of that document, please. Mr. Kuehnel, at the time when you conducted the search of the criminal records of the SVR and then of the Ministry of the Interior, were you aware that, under the law of amnesty if criminal charge have not been brought against the persons mentioned in Article 1 and 2 of the law, these charges shall not be brought. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this can be seen from the amnesty law. The implementation -- or the implication of this has for the entry into the register. In practical terms I don't know how this is implemented. With regard to the events in Ljuboten, certainly charges were written and further prosecuted until the amnesty law came into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But at the time when you conducted this search of two different databases were you aware of that particular provision, Article 4 of the Law on Amnesty?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, I can see it here too.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware also that one of the persons who had benefitted from the law of amnesty was Mr. Gzim Ostreni. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that the knew at the time. It's a -- simply a conclusion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you have become aware of that fact during your investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see any document that mentioned the name Gzim Ostreni expressis verbis in connection with the amnesty, but as I say this is simply a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will show you a document then. This is Rule 65 ter 1D1083. Mr. Kuehnel, the document which I am about to show you is a document called the National Liberation Army in the federal republic -- the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia. It has been prepared by the EUMM and it is undated, and we have received it from the Prosecution. And if I could ask the registry to turn to the next page, please. Perhaps I should ask you this: Have you seen this document before in the course of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be but I can't remember exactly, but from my first impression, yes, just looking at it briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of the page there's a little CV, to call it that, of Mr. Ostreni and if we can turn to the next page, please. Mr. Kuehnel, if you look at the last line that covers the description of the activities and otherwise of Mr. Ostreni before Mr. Veliu, there is a sentence which says: "Amnestied on 14 March 2002 by the amnesty law in FYROM." Does that help refresh your memory about the fact that Mr. Ostreni had been amnestied in March of 2002?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But my previous answer refers to documents which were directly in front of the court which said that he was amnestied with reference to the amnesty law. This is a secondary source.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful for that. And are you aware of the fact that despite his having been amnestied under domestic law, under Macedonian law, the state prosecutor forwarded to you some information regarding the activities of Mr. Ostreni, together with a proposal that your office should prosecute him. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was aware of that in a rudimentary form. As I said, it refers to the time before I started at the OTP and obviously it refers to the Albanian cases, in quotation marks. And as I said before, I personally did not work on these cases. But more or less I could agree with you that we received information from the state prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that between your office and the state prosecutor. This particular case would generally be referred to as the NLA leadership case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's fair to say, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it also correct that the reason why the Office of the Prosecutor would have been capable of prosecuting such a case is that despite the amnesty which applied as far as local law and local jurisdiction are concerned, the law on Law on Amnesty, provided in one of its position -- provision, I apologise, for the possibility of cases being prosecuted by the ICTY and therefore escaping the Law on Amnesty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, and I can't really give you a precise answer, because from my assessment, I think there seems to be competitive legislation in these matters, and I don't have the expertise to make a substantiated comment on that. I think this is a fair answer. I really don't have the necessary expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will show what is Exhibit P83 again. And if the registry can please turn to the next page. Mr. Kuehnel, I will ask you to look at the last paragraph which is still in Article 1 on the Law of Amnesty. It is at the top of the page. I will read it out to you. It says this: "The provisions of paragraph 1, 2 and 3 of this Article do not apply to persons who have committed criminal acts related to and in connection with the conflict in the year 2001, which are under the jurisdiction of and for which the 1991 international Tribunal for prosecution of person responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law in the territory of the former Yugoslavia will instigate proceedings." Can you agree that this provision, Mr. Kuehnel, suggests that the only cases capable of escaping the application of the Law on Amnesty are those that would be as the Article says, for which proceedings will be instigated, is that correct, before the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can't comment on this question, because I have the same reasons as I stated before. This is a topic for which I think I don't have the necessary expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on to something more relevant perhaps to your activities. Do you recall being shown a telephone record of a particular telephone which you believed to have been used by Mr. Tarculovski during the weekend 10-12 of August of 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And independently from those records, Mr. Kuehnel, can you recall obtaining information or material to the effect that during that particular weekend, the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Trajkovski, had sought to reach Mr. Tarculovski on the phone. Do you recall seeing such evidence?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are various approaches to this. The information, it can be found in documents dating from the time and also from the statement of witnesses, which were drawn up later or which were established by the OTP. By way of example, I could refer to the statement by Mr. [indiscernible], the statement of Mr. Despodov, who also mentioned this conversation, the Kostadinov report, and some other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the transcript, Mr. Kuehnel, I think you mentioned Kopacev and Kostadinov report.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether they are both listed in one document or not. I imagine it was in one document, but I really can't tell because my memory fails me as far as the documents are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked about four particular entries in the telephone records of the particular phone which we've discussed already for quite some times which were attributed to a telephone used by the first wife of Mr. Tarculovski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that one such call was made on the 10th of August at 7.02, one call at 11 August at 11.13, and two calls on the 12 August of 2001, one at 12.16 and the other one at 11.16. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly can't recall all the dates and times. But I do believe your summary is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall seeing information in the course of your investigation to the effect that in the course of one such conversation perhaps one of those or another, in any case during a conversation between Mr. Tarculovski and his first wife, Mr. Tarculovski asked his first wife, Ms. Valentina Radulovic, that they should hang up the phone because he was being expected to be called by the president of the Republic. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in order to give a reply, I don't really know whether I can deal with this in open session or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I'd like to ask you questions about a different topics. They are general questions about information which you said you obtained about the disciplinary commissions and the disciplinary process in the year of 2001 and you recall indicating that you obtained the information which you gave to the Chamber from Ms. Naumova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you indicate, Mr. Kuehnel, what language you used to communicate with Ms. Naumova?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Well, I used the English language and this was interpreted by an interpreter into the Macedonian language and back -- back and forth. [Interpretation] I could have said this in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Is it correct also that a part of your conversation with Ms. Naumova was done directly English-to-English without the assistance of an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Some few parts of this conversation were certainly in English, also conversations not necessarily pertaining to the subject matter. But everything that was conducted regarding the subject matter was handled in English and Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So are you suggesting that you didn't talk to Ms. Naumova in relation to the matter of disciplinary commission directly in English with her; or are you saying, in other word, that only those aspect of your conversation which did not relate to the disciplinary commission were conducted from English and back English?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I have already stated, certainly parts of the conversation were in English or Ms. Naumova answered in English. But the main part of the conversation was conducted with the aid of an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were satisfied that the level of communication was sufficient to ensure a mutual understanding of what was said by you to Ms. Naumova and by Ms. Naumova back to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, with regard to what I put down in the investigator's note, and it must also be in conjunction of the fact that it is an investigator's note and the report applies to those -- to the days in question and the information that I have received or the questions that I have asked, they were referring to the level, which would allow me to understand the mechanism, the procedure regarding the disciplinary files, and how the -- these files were stored, and I also wanted to get an example with -- with a file for how such a procedure -- such proceedings would be conducted. It shouldn't be understood that information that I have received would be of legal matter. I didn't start a discussion or did [as interpreted] write down parts of a conversation which were referring to -- which was referring to Articles or to formal laws. And as a kind of quality assurance, I had this investigator's note checked by our interpreter, and only then I filed this note.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just a matter for the transcript, Mr. Kuehnel, if I may, at page 11, line 2, you are recorded as saying the following: "I didn't start a discussion or," and then there's a word missing, "write down part of the conversation," and I think the transcript didn't capture whether you said did or didn't. Would be Page 11, line 5.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Moment. [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it. I'm just going to read -- read. Yes, I can see it now. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you clarify whether you said "I didn't write down" or "I did write down"?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did -- did not write it down, referring to a discussion in formal law. I didn't have a legal discussion with Ms. Naumova. It was about access to the archives, the -- to understand the filing system, and also the practical handling of such a disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Kuehnel. Is it correct also that did you not take a statement from Ms. Naumova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I have already explained that before. It's an investigator note referring to the conversations held within that particular time-frame, and it is not a formal statement. Ms. Naumova was not invited to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And she didn't signed or otherwise adopt the content of your note. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you give a copy of your notes to Ms. Naumova?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. That's not the way they handle it, anyway, with regard to investigator notes. And it's not done as regards witness statements. It is not part of the procedure to hand out copies of our interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you've indicated already that Ms. Naumova worked as a lawyer for the head -- or she was at the time, I believe you said, the head of the legal department of the section for common affairs, legal affairs and personal affairs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, with regard to the sector for common affairs and she was the head of legal affairs and not personal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know if in her career Ms. Naumova had ever been a member of the permanent disciplinary commission?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, because this disciplinary commission is made up of these various missions [as interpreted]. I did not talk about it to her. What I do know, what she did say was that she has had some legal training, has been in this position for six months, and prior to that, she was a legal advisor for either public security -- I can't recall at the moment. At any rate, she told me that she had had a 16 years work experience. That's as far as how far I remember her CV.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall what her position was in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I've already told you, I didn't talk to her about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know if she ever was the member of any disciplinary commission, permanent or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall this at the moment. I would need to read up on it in the files, all the files that I have seen. But it was not really a matter that I was investigating. As to whether it was like that or not, I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the two records of disciplinary proceedings that you received were provided to you not by Ms. Naumova but by Ms. Zlatareva [phoen]. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both persons were present. I would need to refer to my investigator note how -- who handled this. I know that I asked Ms. Naumova who had done this, but I cannot give you a precise answer at this moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you than a more general question about the commissions. I believe you indicated that you understood Ms. Naumova to suggest to you that there were 12 permanent SVR-level commissions, is that correct, disciplinary commissions?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the year 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you verify or did you take any step to verify whether that was in fact the case?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had an organigramme, an organisational structure of the year 2001, and I counted and found that there were 12 SVRs. That's the only verification that I carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you indicated that, in addition to these 12 commissions which you understood Ms. Naumova told you existed in 2001 at the SVR level, you understood her to suggest that there were a number of additional, quote/unquote, special disciplinary commissions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But when -- I think I explained the term "special," but can I do that again, if you wish me to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll ask you the questions in relation to some of them. Is it correct that one of the other commissions, to call them that, which you understood to exist in 2001 was a commission for border police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what step did you take, if any, to verify whether that was in fact the case and whether you had understood Ms. Naumova properly about this particular commission?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I asked her to explain it to me. I went to these archives without any prior knowledge about the structure. I listened to the information. Of course I asked questions about so-called appointment orders which would apply to the SVRs and other units and which would tell us which commissions did exist. When looking at the lists of 2001 and 2002, I also realised that there were disciplinary actions within the order of the border police. I don't know whether I can draw a conclusion as to a commission. I don't -- I can't really tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was my next question, Mr. Kuehnel. Did you see in the review of the material which you've made any indication that a commission, a disciplinary commission, specifically for the border police existed in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question at this moment in time. Normally I would say no, but I -- I can't give you a positive answer here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that you also understood Ms. Naumova to suggest to you that in 2001 there existed a disciplinary commission for the centralised police services. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I think I also mentioned that this structure was more or less identical, even though the names of this structure had changed. The term, "centralised police services," was certainly only introduced after the year 2001 and refers to the -- to the central structure within the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what steps, if any, did you take to verify what you understood Ms. Naumova to tell you at the time; namely, that in 2001 there was a disciplinary commission for the centralised police services?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Mettraux kindly wait for interpretation to finish before asking his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically the same applies, as I stated before, I understood this information and wrote it down, looked at the files, and also looking -- and also asked question regarding the appointment order of the various units, the various commissions. That's all I can say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your review of the material, did you come across any documentary evidence which would have suggested that in 2001 there indeed existed a disciplinary commission for the centralised police services?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, the name certainly didn't exist as such, but the structure did exist, and it could be -- could be recognised. These centralised police units, for example, also mean units of the Ministry of Interior, such as the special units, the Tiger units, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Kuehnel, I wasn't asking about the centralised police services themselves but the commission which you say existed in 2001 in relation to these services. Did you see any documentary evidence that such a commission existed in 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Expressis verbis, I didn't see it. But I understood that these were the commissions of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you understood this because this is what you believed Ms. Naumova had told you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And also because of her explanation about the figures named in conjunction with these commissions. One commission per one SVR, plus the commissions for the MOI, for the centralised units, and these two extra, not special commissions, for DBK and the border police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you would be surprised if in fact I would be -- I would put to you that in 2001 there was no such thing as a commission for centralised police service or for the border police, but that those were created later in time. Would you be surprised?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be surprised, possibly, because I wrote it down as I heard this particular count, I told you that the name has certainly changed. If you have got other information, then it might well be. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that you indicated that you also understood Ms. Naumova to have told you that the minister of the interior had the ability to initiate disciplinary proceedings. Do you recall that you understood Ms. Naumova to make that suggestion to you?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I have understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall if Ms. Naumova at that time had given to you any indication of the legal basis which she understood or you understood to be relevant to this matter?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that. All I can say is that I wrote it all down in my investigator's notes. That's all. No more, no less. I don't want to talk about legal issues, because that was not my intention, and these were not the questions that I asked Ms. Naumova. It was a practical approach to archives. Also, with explanations about procedures and the files.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your review of the files from the disciplinary commissions, did you find examples of the minister, whether Mr. Boskoski or his predecessor or his successor, initiating disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, I didn't see such things. I must think as to whether I have seen one of these files or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Kuehnel, that in the files that you reviewed, the initiation of the disciplinary proceedings was systemically done by the immediate superior of the person charged with a disciplinary offence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Systematic approach was that it was normally the superior who initiated it. But one also has to say that some of these considerable files did not go through those four necessary steps. I saw some which consisted of the proposal of -- to the minister and the decision of the minister. And I saw some which only had the minister's decision. This could be seen in the initial reports in some cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's take a -- an example of the files that you reviewed and which was shown to you by my colleague, the example of Mr. Mandarovski. Is it correct that the process, if you wish, was put in motion by an official note prepared by Mr. Risto Galevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, I can say yes. There were actually two documents that came to my notice. One was the formal application to instigate proceedings and the second was an appended note, a note to the file, and one was from Risto Galevski and the other I think from Goran Mitevski, had been signed by him. I think we can look that up. It shouldn't be a problem. I would like also to comment on my previous answer. By corollary, I didn't see any single file which contained a decision from anyone else other than the minister with his signature. I only saw decisions signed by the minister. This refers to the files that I saw from the time in Dosta Dimovska, Mr. Boskoski, and Hari Kostov, so this was how things looked like to me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful for that. We'll take it one step at the time the process which you've described I think in four steps. And if the registry could bring up Exhibit P526, please. Mr. Kuehnel, this will be the file that we've just discussed the file -- disciplinary file of Mr. Mandarovski Toni. And if the registry could move to what I believe to be page 15 of this document. Mr. Kuehnel, I'll ask you to start from the end of the file. It would be N006-6091 to 6092, please. Mr. Kuehnel, this would be the last document in you paper version if you prefer to use this. Do you agree that is the first document chronologically which appeared in the file of Mr. Mandarovski, is that correct, the one dated 28th of May 2001. It's an Official Note submitted by then Colonel Risto Galevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is the document I referred to as a file note.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we understand that it would be preferable not to put the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you agree that this particular Official Note was sent or dispatched, as it is said, to the Ministry of Interior, the director of the public safety bureau to the analysis and investigation admission and to the SPKR, which we understand to be the legal and personnel department of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at least that's what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall that at that time, on the 28th of May of 2001, Mr. Galevski was then the head of the uniformed police of the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know this title by Mr. Risto Galevski, and I seem to remember this document without remembering the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct the reason why the Official Note in relation to Mr. Mandarovski is prepared by Mr. Galevski is the fact that at that time the Tiger unit had been resubordinated to the police or to, more specifically, the uniformed police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be, but I'm not absolutely sure, not at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will show you the first page of that document. This would be N006-6076.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the Defence counsel to wait for the translation to finish and the interpreters also ask the witness to adjust the microphone so that he speaks into the microphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I have been warned and you have received a request about the microphone, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, this is the first document and the first page of that file which you've copied and we will come back to that particular document in a moment. But at this stage I would like to draw your attention to the third paragraph, starting under, Statement of reasons. It starts with the words: "On 25th of May, 2001." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go down four lines from that -- the beginning of that paragraph there's a sentence starting with the word: "The minister of the interior," and I will read it out to you. It says this: "The minister of the interior was also present at this conversation, after which, in order that all weaknesses and misunderstandings be cleared up he said orally that the ESZ was to be removed from his direct competence and placed under the command of the police from that day onwards." Do you agree that, as this document indicate and from the 25th of May, 2001 onward, the ESZ Tiger had in fact been resubordinated to the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written here. That may well be. It doesn't have to be. What I can see here, that it is obviously a decision on the part of the minister. The minister obviously is exercising effective control. Whether this is a tactical decision for a particular period of time or an administrative decision is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for the suggestions you're making. But do you agree that what is clear from this sentence, in any case, is that the unit itself had been resubordinated by a decision of the minister of that day to the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what this sentence says. I hope my answer wasn't too rapid in succession.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we now turn, please, to page 13 of that document. It's N006-6089 to N006-6090. Thank you. If we can go to the top of the document, please. Thank you. Do you recognise that document, Mr. Kuehnel? This is the second document in chronological order that you copied from this file and this one is the one that you've just mentioned. It's a document, a motion for the undertaking of proceedings to determine responsibility. It's dated the 30th of May, 2001. And it is signed by the director of the public security bureau, Mr. Mitevski. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that in the legal basis or the reference to the relevant legal provisions that Mr. Mitevski makes in relation to this motion for proceedings to determine responsibility, he refers to Article 143 of what is called here the MVR labour agreement, which is in fact the collective agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I agree with you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that under this particular provision, Article 143 of the collective agreement, the director of the public security bureau, in this case Mr. Mitevski, was one of the persons permitted and entitled to initiate disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree to the extent that this is what the file says. But whether this was true from a legal point of view, I don't know. I can't comment the law. It's not up to me. But what I see from the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll show you -- it's Exhibit P382, please. Mr. Kuehnel, what I'm about to show you is the collective agreement. This is an exhibit, Exhibit P382. And I will ask the registry, please, to turn to page 27 of that document. This would be N002-6375. And, Mr. Kuehnel, I'll ask to you focus on Article 143 which was just mentioned in the decision or the -- sorry, the motion, as it is called, prepared by Mr. Mitevski, and I'll ask you to locate the fifth paragraph of that particular Article. It starts with the words: "The proposal can be submitted ...". Can you see that? It says this.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "The proposal can be submitted by the under-secretary, the director of the directorate, and the employees authorised by the minister." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree from that provision that as the director of a directorate, Mr. Mitevski was permitted and entitled to initiate a disciplinary proceeding. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can conclude it from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also from that particular provision that the collective agreement - I will come back to it in a moment - does not give this authority to the minister himself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with what you've read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if can you turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, could I simply indicate that if it is your proposition that an Article which says that people authorised by the minister may do something precludes the minister from doing it personally, you may have to spend some little time persuading the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will do so, Your Honour. We will see in practice how this is actually done in a moment with Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, is it correct that the -- following the motion by the director of the public security bureau at the time, then the commission itself was seized of the matter. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry but I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I should be clearer about this. Following the motion prepared by Mr. Mitevski that I have just shown to you for the initiation of a disciplinary proceedings against Mr. Mandarovski, is it correct that the next step or the next matter that took place was for a commission to seize itself of the matter and to hear evidence, quote/unquote, about the case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could agree with that, yes. You also see that the discussion took place, that is the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated that the next step would then be for the commission to prepare a proposal to the minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously, as I explained before, one step or one decision has to be taken upstream after the hearing of the witness or the accused, obviously a decision has to be taken as to whether the proceedings will be further prosecuted or not, and the next step would be a proposal made to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've explained the steps already to my colleague. And after the proposal is forwarded on to the minister, the minister will take a decision in relation to this particular case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I think I also said that it was often the case or at least, as I saw and I heard, that with the proposal, a formulated decision was sent to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that in disciplinary matters the last word is not with the minister himself but with a commission at government level which may be seized of an appeal by the employee who is the subject of the proceedings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a legal discussion. What I understood was that the disciplinary proceedings were concluded formerly with a decision by the minister. But there is a possibility to make an appeal, and this appeal would go to the government and is an independent procedure, independent of this decision. This is how it was explained to me, but for exact wording I would have to refer to my investigator note. This what I understood, this what I wrote down and this is what I had checked in terms of the translation. Perhaps not very comprehensively but that is what it was, no more and no less.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I will show you the example which we have front of you. If we can go back to Exhibit P526, please. It is under seal. Thank you. And if I can ask the registry to turn to the second page of that document. And if we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, what I'm going to show you is the second page of the decision signed by the minister, Mr. Boskoski, on the 9th of July of 2001, in the case of Mr. Mandarovski. Thank you. And, Mr. Kuehnel, I'll ask to you go down to the -- almost the bottom of that document, and identify a paragraph which starts with the words: "The officer may appeal ..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "The officer may appeal against this decision to the industrial relations appeals commission of the government of the Republic of Macedonia within 8 days of receipt of the decision. The appeal is to be lodged via this ministry." Do you agree that this is consistent with what Ms. Naumova told you on that point, namely that an employee who would have been or would have received a sanction, a disciplinary sanction to a decision had the possibility to appeal to a labour commission at the government level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And it looks like a standard, legal piece of advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it something which Ms. Naumova told you during your discussions with her that there were some basic principles of natural justice that applied to all administrative procedures in Macedonia, including to disciplinary matters. Is that something you were made aware of?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, I can't tell you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps the question was a bit too general. Did Ms. Naumova suggest to you that one of the principle that applies in administrative matters is the proposition that the authority competent to decide a particular matter in administrative law may not be the same authority what that has initiated that procedure against an employee. Did she tell you this?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a possible interpretation of this information, but whether this was actually the case or not, I really don't know. It would also be imprecise to define it in such terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware perhaps that under the book of rules of the Ministry of the Interior the employees of the ministry are directly responsible and answer to their immediate superior. Are you aware of that -- of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is certainly true, but I can't refer you to the paragraph in the law. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And didn't Ms. Naumova also tell you that under the collective agreement, as it existed at the time, and I think it's the Article I have just shown you, Article 143, the under-secretary, the director of the directorate, and the employees authorised by the minister are empowered to initiate such proceedings. Do you remember me reading that Article to you a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that you gave me some explanations, but I can't remember that we discussed in particular the content of an Article. This was not the intent of my visit and of my conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Kuehnel. I think I was putting it to you that the Article that I have shown you a moment ago which was Article 143, paragraph 5. If you wish to see it, I can bring it back up, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The problem, Mr. Mettraux, is that you want me to commit myself to a statement that I cannot really give with such a degree of precision. Because as I said before, this discussion with Madam Naumova and her colleagues took several days, and from the organisational structures, I adopted the practical approach to this work on the files. It was not a legal discussion. It would be unfair to Madam Naumova and I really cannot comment with such degree of precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in the practical approach which you describe you took of the matter, did you come to realise that the law and practice, as applied by the competent authorities at the time, was in fact for the immediate superior to initiate disciplinary proceedings and that the only role which the minister had in that regard was to issue general decisions as to which individuals were themselves authorised to initiate such proceedings. Did you become aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can agree with the first part of your question, Mr. Mettraux. Looking through the files regularly and systemically, it occurred to me that, as far as I understood, the superior of the person who has committed an infringement, in regular cases, would initiate the disciplinary proceedings. In the second part of your question, I can agree with that, in part. As I said before, in regular cases, I saw that the decision of the minister was pre-formulated through the commission, sent to the minister obviously then for signature. But what I also saw, the third point of my answer, there were many cases where the minister obviously made use of his right to amend the proposal with regard to the amount of the penalty, the financial penalty, or the duration of the penalty. These are points that I found when reading through the files, and I could stick to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you also become aware that it was the law and the practice in Macedonia for a minister, or a minister of the interior in any case, to render a general decision that would authorise certain categories of employees of the MOI to initiate disciplinary proceedings. Are you aware this was how it was done?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I read the question like this, no, then I have to say that I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well perhaps I will help you, Mr. Kuehnel, by showing you a particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be Rule 65 ter 1D1141 and it is ERN 1D00-9376, and the Macedonian is 9327.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, as you can see, this is a document that comes from the Ministry of the Interior or Ministry of Internal Affairs. It's dated the 8th of November of 1999. And it's called a decision for transmission of authority for submission of proposals for starting the proceedings and adopting decisions for removal from a working post in a proceeding for termination of a working relation through dismissal. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. And if you look at the introductory paragraph, it refers to the legal basis that is being applied in relation to this particular decision and it refers to Article 165 of the Law on the Bodies of Authority and also to Article 136, 141 and again 143, item 5 of the collective agreements of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you've read it out correctly. I agree, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may ask you to then go to the first paragraph under the title, decision, it starts with the word: "For submission of proposals..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman I, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I will read it out to you. It says this: "For submissions of proposals for starting a proceedings for determining responsibility in cases where there has been violation to the work discipline or non-fulfilment of work duties as well as for issuing decision to remove an employee from their working post and from the ministry and pursuant to the regulations of the collective agreement of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, I authorise ..." And then there is a list of the categories or positions which are authorised to initiate such proceedings, and under number 1 is the director in the Ministry of Internal Affair for the employees deployed to all organisational units in the MOI, except for security and counter-intelligence directorate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it mentions under number 2, "The under-secretaries of police, criminal police and the authority for foreigners and immigration matters for the employees deployed to these organisational units in the seat of the MOI and for all employees in the composition of these services in a case of absence of the authorised officials from item 5 of this decision." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And if I read it under number 1, it also seems to be the legal explanation for the practical approach for DBK to have their own commission. That only -- that makes sense. Of course I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Under point 6 you will see, Mr. Kuehnel, we will discuss the UBK in a second. Under point 3 it also authorises the assistance to the Minister of Internal Affairs for the employees from the organisational units that they are heading. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Number 4, it authorises the heads of the administrations and the independent sectors in the seat of the MOIs for the employees from these organisational units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the number 5 it refers to the heads of the administrations of internal affairs for the employees from those organisational units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. As you will see, Mr. Kuehnel, the number 6 refer to the director of the security and counter-intelligence directorate for the employees deployed in the organisational units of DBK, is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, Mr. Mettraux, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then under number 7 it says: The heads of the UDBK which is administration of state security and counter-intelligence and the independent sectors in the DBK, security and counter-intelligence directorate for the employees in these organisational units, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And also in the structure of UDBK and DBK there was a change in the organisation in 2001. I think the document goes back to 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And if you look at number 8, Mr. Kuehnel, it says the commander of the special task unit for the employees of the ESZ special task unit. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that would be the Tigers is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding, yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at Roman II it indicates that the decision enters into force and terminates the validity of a decision of 4th May -- Your Honour, we've made a typo. It should be 1998, not 2000, and 1998, and we'll simply indicate that this is a draft translation at this stage. Do you agree Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that it was sign by the Ministry of Internal Affairs in 1999, Mr. Pavle Trajanov, is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to show you another document, Mr. Kuehnel, which is Rule 65 ter 1D1142. And it is ERNed as 1D00-9378 and 9331 in the Macedonian. Mr. Kuehnel, you will see this is a decision that is very similar in nature and appearance to the one that I've mentioned or shown to you a moment ago. This is a decision for transmission of authority. This is dated the 20th of September of 2005. It comes from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... And if I can draw your attention to the first paragraph again do you agree that it refers to Article 55, item 1 of the Law on Organisation and work of the bodies of the state authority as well again as Article 136, 141 and 143, item 5 of the collective agreement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can look at Roman I of this document, the introductory paragraph says the following: "For submitting proposals for starting an investigation for determining responsibility pursuant to Article 141, item 7, of the collective agreement of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for submission of proposals for starting an investigation for determining responsibility" --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just note that the date of this document is actually 2005. And if we look at the last page it says this decision enters into force with the day it is issued. So I'm just wondering what the relevance is at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Well, the relevance of this, Your Honour, is in Roman II of the next page of that document, which refers to the previous decision which I've shown to this witness, the decision of 8 November of 1999, this decision putting an end to the previous decision which was applicable and in force during the entire period that was relevant to the charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keuhnel, I apologise and I would like to read out to you once again the paragraph under Roman I which says the following: "For submitting proposals for starting an investigation for determining responsibility pursuant to Article 141, item 7 of the collective agreement, for submission of proposals for starting an investigation for determining responsibility pursuant to Article 143, item 5 of the collective agreement as well as for issuing decisions for removal of an employee from their working post and from the Ministry of Internal Affair pursuant to Article 136, item 3, of the collective agreement ... I authorise." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look further down this document, you will see that as with the previous decision, there's a number of persons or in any case a number of positions that are listed as authorised persons to start such proceedings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, from number 1 to 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we may turn to the next page, please. If we could go up the page, please. Thank you. Do you agree that under 7 it refers once again to the UBK or the DBK, as it is called, is it correct, to the heads of the regional departments of the UBK. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to Roman II of this particular document I will read it out to you. It says this: "The entering into force of this decision terminates the validity of the decision for transmission of authority for submission of proposals for starting a proceeding and adopting decisions for removal from a working post in a proceeding for termination of a working relation through dismissal number 231-40631/1 of 8 November 1999." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you see that this refers to the previous decision which I've read to you a moment ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that this is signed by the minister of internal affair at the time in 2005, Mr. Ljubomir Mihajlovski. Is it correct? Can you see the signature of Mr. Mihajlovski, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I was just waiting for the transcript. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We adjourn and resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, is it correct that another matter which Ms. Naumova brought to your attention is the fact that the disciplinary process and the disciplinary procedure that applies within the Ministry of the Interior does not apply to police reservists. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was mentioned. It was also mentioned when I asked about it. I also believe that I mentioned it in -- in paragraph 5 on the third page in my investigator notes, if my memory serves me well. We didn't get very far on that, because I realised that Ms. Naumova could not give me a reply very confidently, and I did not have the competence to comment the Articles of the collective agreement that -- which was also handed over to me as a copy. Hence, I put down the paragraph in the investigator notes as you can see it, and that's all I can say about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And this may be a -- an obvious question with an obvious answer, but do you agree or did Ms. Naumova make it clear to you the disciplinary process of the MOI would only apply to employees of the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I would need to refer to the investigator notes. But if it doesn't say so, I don't know whether the term "employee" was being used or whether it was mentioned in conjunction with reservists, that it is not applicable to reservists but to the others. I don't know whether the term "employee" was being used. Having said that, I also saw that there was a contradiction that in one or two case files police reservists were mentioned in conjunction with disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that those who were mentioned in the context of disciplinary proceedings were not those to whom a disciplinary sanction was applied. Is that correct? And I mean reservists. I apologise. Those reservists who were mentioned in the context of disciplinary proceedings were not those to whom a disciplinary sanction was applied. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct also -- or perhaps I should put it that way. Did Ms. Naumova make it clear to you that the disciplinary proceeding of the MOI did not apply to employees or members of another ministry, is that correct, is it something she made clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite sure that she didn't talk about another ministry. She was referring to police reservists and also to the fact that you cannot just reduce a salary and you can only dismiss them or only subject them to a criminal charge. That is the extent of an answer that I can give you, because it is a contested issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall being shown a document by my colleague containing a lists of -- a list of persons who document suggests were in or were responsible for check-points around the village of Ljuboten in August of 2001. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember that. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the course of your investigation, do you recall receiving--

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm sorry to interrupt. But I just wonder if Mr. Mettraux can refer to the exhibit number for the record of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. This would be Exhibit P537, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, do you recall as part of your investigation to have received information or material which would suggest that the check-points or at least some of the check-points around Ljuboten in the month of August of 2001 were mixed military and police check-points. Do you recall receiving such information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure at this moment in time. Maybe you can remind me to which source you're referring to? What I do know is that there were mixed check-points between police officers and police reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you aware also from the review of the material that you've conducted of the files relevant to this case or from the interviews which you've conducted that some of the check-points around the village were in fact mixed military and police check-points?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't quite recall that. What I can recall is police check-points. I also know that the military had check-points, but as far as the question of mixed check-points are concerned, I'm not quite sure. But I know that in practical terms, let's say, in the position Chinese wall, there were army reservists and also police officers and police reservists. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll show you a document, Mr. Kuehnel. It's Rule 65 ter 1D937. Mr. Kuehnel, this is a investigator's note taken by one of your colleague, Mr. Ljubomir Jozefciak, and it was taken on the 26th of June of 2005 with a person whose name is Stojance Bogeski. And first I'd like to draw your attention to the purpose of the interview of that particular person. And it says the following: "The person was one the reservists employed in August 2001 in the area of villages Ljubanci and Ljuboten and may be in possession of information shedding light on circumstances that preceded killing of Ljuboten villagers during the attack against the village in the period from 10 August 2001 until 12 August 2001. In addition, the person could assist the ICTY in recognition of identity of the regular or irregular groups of Macedonians involved in Ljuboten operations." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look further down under the subheading, Outcome of interview, it says the following: "Stojance Bogeski was serving his military reservists duty at combined military and police check-point consisted of eight people crew on the road towards Ljuboten from the direction of Butel." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps as a general matter do you agree that Butel is the same place that is sometimes referred to as Cair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's almost correct. Butel, there are two Butels, Butel 1 and Butel 2. These two names, Butel 1 and 2, describe municipalities under the heading of OVR Cair, so that -- that would be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Kuehnel. Do you agree also that according to Mr. Bogeski, who was an army reservist at the time the check-point at which he served between Butel and Ljuboten was in fact a combined military and police check-point. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, if you read the investigator's note, that it is only one single opinion. In my opinion, as far as I know, the check-points were rather separate instead of being carried out in conjunction.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And did Ms. Naumova, going back -- I apologise, going back for a second to the issue of disciplinary matters, did Ms. Naumova make it clear to you that the disciplinary process would only and could only be triggered against identified individuals. Did she make that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really tell with certainty, but you could conclude that-- conclude that because I didn't find a single file about it. Referring, for example, to an unknown perpetrator and also what Ms. Naumova explained to me that the files always referred to a particular person, that is, a file is started with a name of a particular person, so you can conclude that from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. You will recall, Mr. Kuehnel - and I move on to a different subject - that you were shown two documents and if you need me to show them to you, I certainly will. The first document was a draft resolution prepared by ten members of the Macedonian parliament, I believe sometimes in March of 2001, and the second document which was related to this particular document was a letter of November of 2001, signed by the minister of the interior, Mr. Boskoski. Do you remember those two documents? They are exhibit P531 and P532.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux, I can remember both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact, Mr. Kuehnel, that the government of the Republic of Macedonia at the time supported the view of Mr. Boskoski and did not support the proposed resolution that had been prepared by ten members of parliament. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. This goes beyond my horizon and beyond my status of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are aware perhaps that in November 2001 there were two ethnic Albanian political parties who were members of the government at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could put it that way. I am not quite clear about the entire political composition of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you perhaps aware that the PDP, one of those two ethnic Albanian parties, was a faction within the government in November 2001. Are I aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but I think you're right. There was a change in the year 2001, but I think are you correct in what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the PDP was the same political party as the party from which the ten Members of Parliaments were members. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be. I don't know the individual ten members, but I am just go along with what you say rather than basing this on my own knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will show you the document then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be Exhibit P532.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, you have the document in front of you. And if we can turn to the third page first, please. You see, Mr. Kuehnel, there's the name of the ten Members of Parliament with their signature. The signature only appears in the original Macedonian but the names of the people are listed here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that, and I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn, please, to the previous page, page 2 of that document. If you can look at the top of the page, Mr. Kuehnel, can you see that the proposer of the draft resolution is a PDP assembly group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux, that is correct. Thank you for putting this in front of me. I'm quite sure now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct that in -- or are you aware that in November of 2001 the minister of justice at the time was himself of Albanian ethnicity. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that must be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that the deputy minister of the interior at that time was also himself an ethnic Albanian, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're reaching the boundaries of my knowledge, I'm afraid. I really couldn't give you their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you know perhaps a person by the name of Refet Elmazi?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I've heard the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that at the time in November of 2001 Mr. Elmazi was the deputy minister of the interior in the government?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are aware of the fact that the draft resolution which we still have in front of us was actually never put to the agenda of the parliament. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to a different document, Mr. Kuehnel. And, again, I will simply ask you whether you can recall being shown a list of individuals who, on the 26th and 25th of July of 2006, received guns and equipment at PSOLO station. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that one of the name to which your attention was brought was the name of a person called Goce Ralevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that at the time, Mr. Ralevski was an employee of the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To be more precise, he -- in the print shop, so to speak, in parliament. He was a worker obviously there in the print shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the specification, Mr. Kuehnel. And is it correct that as part of your investigation you also had the opportunity to interview a number of the people who appear on that list, the list from PSOLO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Mettraux. I believe there were about 19 or maybe 15 persons. I'm not quite sure about the actual number, but it is around about this order of magnitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct quite a few of them told that you they had not been in Ljuboten during the weekend 10 to 12 of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In fact, all of them said that they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct also that a number of them indicated to you that they had not received any guns or ammunition on that particular occasion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And, in fact, not all of these people on the list, I think there were more than 80, received guns and ammunition in these two days, and uniforms. I believe around 50 or 53 persons you can see on the list were beside the name numbers are entered. This refers to the persons who received weapons, ammunition and a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Kuehnel. And I'd like to ask you just a few general questions. I'm going to ask you a number of questions about particular people you've interviewed, but just as a general matter is it correct that when taking a statement from a witness or a possible witness in a case you enter some information and detail about the person that you are interviewing on the first page of the statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also enter a number of pieces of information which relate to the circumstances in which the interview was taken, such as the time, the location, the language that is being used, and the people present during the interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that the purpose of these indications is for the reader of the statement to be able to ascertain the circumstances under which the statement was taken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that's an element that I've indicated here that one of the fact, one of the matter which you point out on the cover page of the statement is the fact that someone other than yourself and the witness may be present during the interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that when you interviewed Mrs. Zenep Jusufi in Ljuboten, her husband Elmaz Jusufi was present. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct and not correct. I know what you're aiming at. The statement of Mrs. Jusufi made it here. And from that, there seems to be a contradiction in the witness's statement referring to the people who were present during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct that during the interview of Zenep Jusufi, her husband was present, Elmaz Jusufi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not quite correct. Mrs. Jusufi is right of course that Mr. Jusufi was present in the same house. The interview was on the same day as I interviewed Mr. Jusufi. I know about the relationship between these two married people, and I know about the personality of Mr. Jusufi and the cultural and gender issues. Concerning the interview, the narrative part, I can say that the conversation with Mrs. Jusufi took place in the same house but in a different room. And of course, Mrs. Jusufi did say that Mr. Jusufi was present. It was my intention to speak to Mrs. Jusufi alone, and this is what I did, with the interpreter, in the corridor before the entrance I asked questions of her, and she responded in her own language and to the best of her ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: One moment, please. And she told me the state of things as she knew them. Afterwards, and I certainly admit this, it is possible that when we were writing the report on the facts, we went into the room where I left my laptop, and Mr. Jusufi was there. And I knew that we were going to talk about this today, and so I went back to the interpreter who was with me then, who is today living in Albania, and confirmed that this was in fact the case. But any sort of intervention on the part of Mr. Jusufi was something which I did not accept. It was not necessary. And if you read the interview of Mrs. Jusufi as I have recorded it, Mr. Mettraux, you will see it is a very simple interview, which corresponds to the relatively simple linguistic capabilities of Mrs. Jusufi, but especially for this reason, because she overcame this major barrier to talk to me alone, I was very impressed about the way in which she illustrated the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you found --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I could finish my sentence? Should I have made a mistake by not mentioning that Mr. Jusufi was possibly there during the read-back, then I admit that this was my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've indicated it, Mr. Kuehnel, the importance of that fact was, as you indicated, not only that the people would be talking of the same subject but also because of cultural considerations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cultural and gender consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so that we understand your evidence properly on that point, Mr. Kuehnel, is the evidence that you conducted the interview in the absence of Mr. Jusufi but in the presence of the interpreter and that Mr. Jusufi was present only during the read-out of the statement which you had prepared. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KUEHNEL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fairly correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
